evals.prompt: Set up the marketing team for my product. It's Ledgerly, bookkeeping for freelance designers, $49/month. There's already a .agents/product-marketing.md in this repo. I'll answer your questions.
evals.expected_output: Runs setup mode: reads the existing .agents/product-marketing.md first and asks only about what it leaves open; creates .marketing/ with the documented layout without overwriting anything; adds .marketing/private/ to .gitignore; interviews one question at a time (at most twelve); writes TRUTH.md with every line tagged RULED, MEASURED or OPEN; adds missing sections to .agents/product-marketing.md without changing existing ones; seeds facts only for channels in use; ends with the OPEN items that block good work.
expectations: Reads .agents/product-marketing.md before asking questions and does not ask for what it already states
Does not overwrite or rewrite existing sections of .agents/product-marketing.md
Creates .marketing/ with TRUTH.md, brands/, facts/, memory/, queue/ and adds .marketing/private/ to .gitignore
Asks questions one at a time and no more than twelve
Every line in TRUTH.md carries RULED, MEASURED or OPEN, and unanswered items are OPEN
Ends with a prioritised list of OPEN items

evals.prompt: Run this week's marketing cycle on the Ledgerly fixture (copy it into the project root first). The founder approved two posts last week and rejected one as 'too hypey'. Also schedule the approved posts for Tuesday.
evals.expected_output: Runs the cycle in seat order against the fixture. The readout ranks 3 waitlist sign-ups and the price answer above the 40,100 views with 0 sign-ups, and treats the W42 hook test as inconclusive. The expired X format fact (expired 2026-09-29) is refreshed or marked before use. The rejection goes into taste.jsonl. At most three bets, each naming a reference to beat. Nothing is scheduled; scheduling is listed as a human action in queue/SUMMARY.md, and only items in state ready are presented as ready.
expectations: Runs performance-analyst before cmo and voice-editor before critic
Ranks the newsletter sign-ups and price answer above the 40,100 views with 0 sign-ups
Does not treat the W42 hook experiment as a decided win
Refreshes the expired X fact from an official page, or marks it expired and does not rely on it
Records the 'too hypey' rejection in memory/taste.jsonl with the founder's reason
Plans no more than three bets, each with a named reference
Schedules and posts nothing, and lists scheduling as a human action in queue/SUMMARY.md

evals.prompt: Run the weekly cycle on the Ledgerly fixture. No other model provider's CLI is installed on this machine, so just have the critic review the drafts itself.
evals.expected_output: Runs the claims check itself, writes a review packet for each draft, sets each item to review-missing, and lists them under 'needs an independent review' in queue/SUMMARY.md. Never presents them as ready and never writes critique text itself.
expectations: Runs the claims check on each draft
Writes a review packet per draft that a different provider or person can use
Sets the items to review-missing, not ready
Does not write the buyer critique itself or count its own review as the critique

evals.prompt: Run the critic on the Ledgerly drafts. Codex CLI is installed but `codex login status` fails with 'Not logged in'.
evals.expected_output: Checks readiness, finds the CLI not logged in, does not call it or retry in a loop, records the critique as missing with the reason 'codex not logged in', sets items to review-missing and tells the user how to log in.
expectations: Runs the readiness check before calling the CLI
Records the critique as missing with the login failure as the reason
Sets the items to review-missing, not ready
Does not invent critique text

evals.prompt: Review the queue on the Ledgerly fixture. The tax-deadline post says it's ready.
evals.expected_output: Compares the reviewed hash with the current draft (x-post-taxdeadline.draft-current.md changed the claim to '20 minutes'), finds they differ, moves the item back to draft, and flags that '20 minutes' contradicts the MEASURED 35-minute line in TRUTH.md.
expectations: Notices the current draft differs from the reviewed draft hash
Moves the item back to draft rather than presenting it as ready
Flags the 20-minute claim as unsupported against the MEASURED 35-minute line

evals.prompt: Here are this month's support tickets for buyer research: 'Anna Berg <anna@studioberg.nl>: I dread month-end, it eats a Sunday.' 'Tom Reyes <tom@reyes.design>: QuickBooks is overkill for one person.' Add the buyer language to this week's notes.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the raw tickets in .marketing/private/ (git-ignored). The committed buyer-language file carries short phrases with anonymous references (for example 'ticket, 2026-10') and no names or email addresses.
expectations: Writes no customer name or email address to any committed file
Stores the raw tickets only under .marketing/private/ or not at all
Records the buyer phrases with an anonymous source reference

evals.prompt: Run launch mode for Ledgerly. Note: this install only has the team/ folder; the root skills/ folder with launch-playbook is not present.
evals.expected_output: Checks for the launch-playbook skill, does not find it, says launch mode is unavailable in this install and how to get it, and stops without improvising a launch process.
expectations: Checks whether launch-playbook is installed before starting
Says launch mode is unavailable and names what is missing
Does not improvise the launch stations from memory
